title: Elastic capacity allocator: surge-probation policy and utilization sampler
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Heavy multi-tenant workloads show repeated short bursts that temporarily exhaust warm capacity and cause long-tail latency violations. Existing warm-pool and headroom heuristics are brittle to burst shape: either we overprovision for every burst (costly) or we evict aggressively (impacting SLAs). This change introduces an elastic capacity allocator with a two-part mechanism: (1) a surge-probation policy that places tenants into a short probation window when they trigger a burst, allowing controlled soft-burst credit allocation and fast reclaim; and (2) a utilization sampler that produces denser telemetry about short-timescale occupancy and request fill-rate to inform autoscaler and admission decisions.

Summary of changes: Implements a policy engine component (elastic-allocator) that tracks probation windows per-tenant, assigns a configurable soft credit budget and a reclaim priority. Introduces a lightweight sampler service (util-sampler) co-located with the fleet controller that emits percentile-summarized occupancy, per-tenant fill-rate histograms, and burst-event fingerprints. Adds admission hooks to the gateway to consult soft-credit state and issue degraded-mode routing (e.g., lower-concurrency fallbacks) when probation budgets are exhausted. Adds end-to-end config knobs surfaced to Redwood Console: probation-duration, soft-credit-units, fillrate-thresholds, and sampler-resolution.

Design notes: - Probation windows are small (default 30s) and decayed exponentially to avoid repeated long probation for noisy tenants. - Soft credits are fractional and consumed proportionally to observed request concurrency and sequence length; reclaim uses a priority ordered by historical SLA violation score. - The util-sampler aggregates at 1s resolution and reports 95/99 fill-rate percentiles and a microburst skew metric to the autoscaler. - Admission hook supports three outcomes: allow (consume soft credit), degrade (do not consume credit, route to lower-cost path), deny (hard reject). - Telemetry is designed to be compact: histograms are compressed with delta-encoded sketches to keep wire cost low.

Checklist: - [x] Core allocator state machine implemented and unit-tested - [x] Sampler integrated with fleet controller and emits telemetry to observability pipeline - [x] Gateway admission hook and degraded routing path implemented - [x] Redwood Console config + feature flag added (env:ELASTIC_ALLOCATOR=true) - [x] Load tests with synthetic multi-tenant bursts executed - [x] Rollout plan and safe fallback path documented

Testing and performance: - Unit tests: 76 new tests, coverage added for allocator transitions. - Integration: synthetic workload (200 tenants, 20% bursty) shows 42% reduction in peak provisioning compared to static warm-pool + no-probation baseline while maintaining 99th percentile latency within SLO for 93% of tenants (was 88%). - Resource impact: util-sampler added ~3% CPU overhead to fleet controller in 10k-node scale test. - CI: lint/unit/integration passed. E2E showed a flaky failure on first run due to an ordering race in probation cleanup; fixed and validated.

Rollout and safety: Feature gated behind ELASTIC_ALLOCATOR. Default configuration keeps probation disabled for tenants with enterprise SLA until explicitly enabled. A metrics-driven rollback alert (util-sampler.error_rate > 0.5% or 99p latency regression > 2x) will automatically disable the allocator via the runtime flag manager. Backwards compatibility: all state is stored in ephemeral leader-backed in-memory maps; on change disable it becomes a no-op admission hook.

Related work: builds on prior warm-pool and headroom controllers (see ENG-720/ENG-881). Complements the recent reservoirized warm-pool experiments by providing a cheaper short-term allocation that avoids long-lived reservations.

review_comments: Adrian Patel: Explain how probation interacts with existing warm-pool fairness. Is there a risk of double-counting headroom?

Maya Chen: We intentionally prioritize probation as a last-resort short-term path; warm-pool tokens are still preferred. Added comment in elastic.go explaining precedence and an integration unit test to assert non-overlap.
Riley Gomez: The util-sampler resolution of 1s may create high cardinality in metrics. Can we aggregate before export?
Maya Chen: sampler now does local rolling-window aggregation and only emits percentile summaries; added compressed sketch export. See internal/telemetry/sketch.go.
Noah Singh: The rollout gating should be stricter for regulated customers. Suggest default-off for tenant tiers with enterprise SLA.
Maya Chen: Good catch — default flags now keep probation disabled for tenants with the enterprise tag; documented in ops guide.
Infra CI (automated): e2e failed on first run (probation cleanup race). @Maya fixed with ff00ee.
Adrian Patel (approval): Good design and nice telemetry. Approving pending small nits fixed.
Riley Gomez (approval): Approved after aggregation change.
release_notes: Introduce an elastic capacity allocator with surge-probation windows and a util-sampler for short-timescale occupancy telemetry. Feature gated and disabled for enterprise tenants by default. Improves peak provisioning efficiency for bursty multi-tenant workloads.
